Yoga with Sandra Leifer: practice and classes

Yoga is a practice that joins movement, breath and attention to the body. Sandra Leifer has experience in several types of yoga and teaches yoga classes. Here is a short introduction to the practice and how to contact her.

Sandra Leifer is an artist and visual-arts teacher. Her biography on this site also lists yoga therapy among her fields.

What is yoga

Yoga is an ancient practice that comes from India. In classes today it is usually presented as a combination of postures (asanas), breathing and relaxation, and sometimes meditation.

Different styles put the emphasis in different places: some have more flowing movement, some long holds of postures, some quiet recovery. That is why it matters to choose a practice that suits you.

Yoga is a practice, not a medical treatment. If you have health problems, an injury or are pregnant, it is worth talking to a doctor before you start.

Common styles of yoga

This is a general overview of yoga styles, not a list of what Sandra teaches. Which styles she leads and in what format, ask her directly on WhatsApp.

  1. Hatha yoga

    A general name for practices with postures and breathing. Usually a calm pace and attention to how each posture is done.

  2. Vinyasa yoga

    Postures are joined into a flowing sequence, and the movement is tied to the breath.

  3. Yin yoga

    A slow practice: passive postures are held for a long time, in relaxation.

  4. Restorative yoga

    A gentle practice with supports (cushions, bolsters, blankets) and an emphasis on rest.

  5. Yoga therapy

    Yoga adapted to the needs of a particular person. It does not replace medical care.

What a yoga class is usually like

A class usually includes a warm-up, postures, breathing exercises and a final relaxation. You need a mat and comfortable clothes.

The format of classes with Sandra, the place, language and time are agreed personally: write to her on WhatsApp.

Yoga and creativity

Sandra is developing her own method of group creative self-exploration, which combines movement, breathing, gesture, artistic improvisation and NeuroGraphica. If this meeting of body practice and drawing appeals to you, have a look at the NeuroGraphica page.
